interactions.label: Which statement best explains why emergency plain film reading uses a two-part a

params.question: Which statement best explains why emergency plain film reading uses a two-part approach — a targeted pass followed by a full systematic read?

answers.text: The systematic read is too slow for emergency departments and must be shortened

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The systematic read should never be omitted or shortened. The two-part approach exists because certain findings demand immediate action, not because the systematic read is too slow.

answers.text: Certain life-threatening findings require immediate action before the full read is completed

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Dangerous findings such as tension pneumothorax or pneumoperitoneum carry immediate clinical actions. The targeted pass detects these first so that intervention is not delayed, while the full systematic read ensures nothing else is missed.

answers.text: Emergency patients cannot remain still long enough for a single complete read

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Patient cooperation is not the reason for the two-part approach. The targeted pass exists because certain dangerous findings must be detected and acted upon before the rest of the read proceeds.

answers.text: The targeted pass and the systematic read use different imaging projections

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both parts are performed on the same film. The distinction is in what you search for — immediate threats first, then everything else — not in the imaging technique.

overallFeedback.feedback: Emergency reading has two parts because certain dangerous findings carry immediate clinical actions. The targeted pass catches these first, and the full systematic read follows to ensure nothing is missed.
Exactly right. Emergency reading couples detection with action. The targeted pass finds life-threatening signs demanding immediate intervention, then the full systematic read catches everything else.

interactions.label: A radiograph of the wrist shows a cortical lucency with sclerotic, rounded margi

params.question: A radiograph of the wrist shows a cortical lucency with sclerotic, rounded margins and callus formation. There is no soft-tissue swelling. What is the most accurate interpretation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: An acute fracture shows a sharp, non-corticated lucent line with adjacent soft-tissue swelling. Sclerotic margins and callus indicate healing, not an acute injury.

answers.text: Old healed fracture not requiring emergency treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Sclerotic (corticated) margins, callus formation, and the absence of soft-tissue swelling are hallmarks of a chronic healed fracture, distinguishing it from the sharp cortical break and soft-tissue swelling of an acute fracture.

answers.text: Pathological fracture through an underlying bone lesion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A pathological fracture occurs through abnormal bone such as tumour or infection, but the features described — sclerotic margins, callus, and no swelling — indicate a normally healed old fracture.
A stress fracture typically shows a band of sclerosis or periosteal reaction without the mature callus and rounded corticated margins seen in a fully healed old fracture.

overallFeedback.feedback: An old healed fracture has sclerotic (corticated, rounded) margins and callus, with no soft-tissue swelling. An acute fracture has a sharp, dark cortical break with adjacent soft-tissue swelling — swelling is the vital clue.

Well done. The acute-versus-chronic fracture distinction rests on three features: cortical margins (sharp vs sclerotic), callus (absent vs present), and soft-tissue swelling (present vs absent). Swelling is the vital clue to acuity.

interactions.label: Cardiomegaly can be reliably diagnosed on a portable anteroposterior ICU chest f

params.question: Cardiomegaly can be reliably diagnosed on a portable anteroposterior ICU chest film.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. A portable ICU film is almost always anteroposterior, which magnifies the heart and mediastinum. This geometric magnification makes the cardiac silhouette appear falsely enlarged. Cardiomegaly should only be diagnosed on a standard posteroanterior erect chest film.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. A portable AP film magnifies the heart and mediastinum due to the anteroposterior projection and short film-cassette distance. True cardiac size can only be assessed on a standard posteroanterior erect film. Never diagnose cardiomegaly from an ICU AP film.

interactions.label: A post-intubation chest film shows the endotracheal tube tip below the carina in

params.question: A post-intubation chest film shows the endotracheal tube tip below the carina in the right main bronchus. The left lung is completely opacified. What is the immediate action?

answers.text: Advance the tube further to secure a deeper airway position

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The tube is already too deep — advancing it further would worsen right main bronchus intubation and leave the left lung collapsed.

answers.text: Withdraw the tube to 3–5 cm above the carina and obtain a repeat film

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. An endotracheal tube in the right main bronchus ventilates only the right lung, causing left-lung collapse. Withdrawing to the correct position (3–5 cm above the carina) and confirming with a repeat film restores bilateral ventilation.

answers.text: Request an urgent CT thorax to evaluate the left-lung opacification

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CT is unnecessary when the cause is clear. The endotracheal tube in the right main bronchus explains the left-lung collapse. Repositioning the tube is the immediate priority.
The left-lung opacification is collapse due to the malpositioned tube, not pneumonia. Correcting the tube position will re-expand the lung.

overallFeedback.feedback: An endotracheal tube in the right main bronchus blocks ventilation of the left lung, causing collapse. The immediate action is to withdraw the tube to 3–5 cm above the carina and confirm correct position with a repeat film.
Correct. When the endotracheal tube enters the right main bronchus, the left lung is not ventilated and collapses. Withdraw the tube to 3–5 cm above the carina and confirm with a repeat chest film.
